originalTitle: Australia news live: Hume sidesteps question over Taylor’s Icac mention saying ‘this is so distant from him’
content: How a tragedy in a homeless camp laid bare regional Australia’s housing crisis Three months ago, a homeless encampment in Wagga Wagga made headlines when a newborn baby died at a nearby riverbank after their mother gave birth in a tent. Since then, the response to the growing crisis has been fractured and confusing and the community is divided on how to manage the camp. Some have jumped in to help, while others have sided with the council in calls to clear it out. Cait Kelly writes about the ways the housing crisis is playing out in regional Australia. PM urged to stand aside special envoy after assault charge The deputy opposition leader, Jane Hume, has called on the prime minister, Anthony Albanese, to take action against his special envoy for defence, veterans’ affairs and northern Australia, Luke Gosling. The MP has been charged over an alleged assault on the Northern Territory’s administrator earlier this month. Hume told ABC’s Insiders it was a “pretty serious charge”. It’s alleged at this stage but the charge has been laid. Anthony Albanese has been very quick to condemn other people and request, in previous lives, that prime ministers stand down their ministers or their senior members of parliament for far less. I think that he should live up to his own high expectations and stand Luke Gosling down. Gosling previously said he could not comment as the matter was before the courts, but thanked his family and vowed to work to serve his constituents. Penny Wong addresses Garma festival: ‘We are not a monoculture and we have never been’ The announcement was delivered before a powerful audience that included senior cabinet ministers Penny Wong, Malarndirri McCarthy and Jason Clare, and Pacific leaders including Timor-Leste’s prime minister, Kay Rala Xanana Gusmão. As the ripples of the announcement spread across Garma, AAP reports, Wong used her address to draw a contrast with those she suggested were trying to divide Australians. At a time when there are those who seek to set us apart, First Nations peoples, with your generosity, remind us our many different stories brought together make us stronger. We are not a monoculture and we have never been. Continuing on from last post … Djawa Yunupingu, leader of the Yothu Yindi Foundation, tied the new council directly to Yolngu law, ancestral obligation and an unbroken connection to Country, and said Yolngu wanted development and opportunity in a way that kept control on Country and in the hands of traditional owners. We have tourism at Bawaka and Banubanu and it is my dream that there will be a five-star resort on this beautiful Country. We have schools that are teaching our young people. We have a Garma Institute that will be our own university and it will hold our knowledge right here. He said the Yolngu people knew every inch of their Country and the council would stand ready to work alongside the army, the navy and the air force to defend it. It will work with the government and with mining companies, any company who wants to do business with us. It will work in partnership with the Northern Land Council for the people. We will be a part of the economic life of this nation whilst never losing who we are and what we stand for. Yunupingu thanked the Northern Land Council and its chair, Matthew Ryan, for protecting Yolngu interests and standing with them as they prepared for the transition, AAP reports. Yolngu leaders in north-east Arnhem Land have announced a powerful new Dilak Land Council, declaring land rights are “coming home” to traditional owners, AAP reports. On a national stage at the Garma festival, revered elder Djawa Yunupingu told leaders, politicians and visitors from across the country on Saturday real power must sit “fully into the hands of landowners”. “I announce today that land rights is coming home to north-east Arnhem Land,” he said to rapturous applause. There will be a new land council in Arnhem Land and it will be called the Dilak Land Council, and it will be the power for our future. The move cements a new Aboriginal authority in one of the most symbolically important parts of the country and signals a fresh push for self-determination on Yolngu terms. Jane Hume has said she will not comment on proceedings at the NSW anti-corruption commission after the federal opposition leader, Angus Taylor, was mentioned at a hearing. He is not accused of wrongdoing and not a specific target of Operation Rosny, which is investigating allegations of corruption against people associated with the NSW Liberals. Asked about the matter, Hume said she feels “this is so distant from him”. Icac should be allowed to go through its processes free of political interference, free of commentary from politicians, and be allowed to run its course. Writing the review into the 2022 election, we specifically said that each division needs to make sure that its constitution is fit for purpose and that that its membership is match-fit to fight elections. I reiterate that point, it is so fundamentally important. But this is an issue for Icac, it’s not something that I can comment on. It’s not something that the leader is involved in, he hasn’t been named, he hasn’t been called, he hasn’t been approached. It’s kind of very distanced, and I think that the Icac should be allowed to do what it needs to do. Deputy Liberal leader says party will not govern in coalition with One Nation Questions over whether the Liberal party would govern with One Nation have continued to follow the opposition as Pauline Hanson’s party grows in popularity. But the deputy Liberal leader, Jane Hume, has brushed off such suggestions. We are not forming a coalition with One Nation. I think we couldn’t be any clearer than that. The Liberals are already in coalition with the National party. That coalition has been the foundation of very successful governments for 80 years now, and it will continue to be so. chineseTitle: 澳大利亚新闻直播：休谟回避了对泰勒提到的 Icac 的质疑，称“这离他太远了”
chineseContent: 无家可归者营地的悲剧如何暴露了澳大利亚地区的住房危机三个月前，沃加沃加的一个无家可归者营地成为头条新闻，一名新生婴儿因母亲在帐篷里生下孩子而死在附近的河岸上。从那时起，对日益严重的危机的应对措施就支离破碎且令人困惑，社区对于如何管理营地也存在分歧。一些人已经介入提供帮助，而另一些人则站在理事会一边，呼吁清理此事。凯特·凯利 (Cait Kelly) 撰写了有关澳大利亚乡村地区住房危机的情况的文章。总理在受到袭击指控后敦促让特使下台 反对派副领袖简·休姆 (Jane Hume) 呼吁总理安东尼·阿尔巴尼斯 (Anthony Albanese) 对他的国防、退伍军人事务和澳大利亚北部特使卢克·高斯林 (Luke Gosling) 采取行动。该议员本月早些时候因涉嫌袭击北领地行政长官而受到指控。休姆告诉美国广播公司的内部人士，这是一项“相当严重的指控”。现阶段有指控，但指控已经提出。安东尼·艾博尼斯（Anthony Albanese）很快就谴责其他人，并在前世要求总理以少得多的理由让部长或高级议员下台。我认为他应该不辜负自己的高期望，让卢克·高斯林失望。高斯林此前表示，由于此事已提交法庭，他无法发表评论，但他感谢他的家人，并发誓将努力为选民服务。黄英贤在加尔马节上发表讲话：“我们不是单一文化，而且从来都不是。”这一消息是在众多强大的听众面前宣布的，其中包括内阁高级部长黄英贤、马拉迪里·麦卡锡和杰森·克莱尔，以及包括东帝汶总理凯·拉拉·萨纳纳·古斯芒在内的太平洋领导人。作为
